title: Tech Note: Using the 4D Method Flowchart Editor

historical_commentary.text: This note introduces 4th Dimension's Flowchart Editor, a lesser-used alternative way to write methods in a visual flowchart style, and suggests situations where it may be preferable to standard text-based method writing; the Flowchart Editor is a niche, largely forgotten classic-4D tool, and its relevance today is limited given the dominance of standard text-based method editing (and, more broadly, the shift to Project Mode and modern code editors) in current 4D development.
related_updates: 4D's Flowchart Editor was a niche classic-language tool for writing methods visually; it saw little adoption relative to standard text-based method writing and is largely forgotten in modern 4D development

Procedures were renamed Methods starting with 4D V6 (1997), the version this note targets, and modern 4D development now centers on text-based Project Mode code editing (introduced v17, 2018) rather than flowchart-style method authoring
